decisions.reason: The particle therapy water phantom is a strategic option in a growing niche, its uncertainty is unresolved because US release only begins in Q1/2019, and keeping it on the market costs little.
Small volume chambers serve rising demand for small-field dosimetry, cost little to keep in the portfolio, and have too short a track record to justify abandonment.
This second small volume chamber partly overlaps with B, but carrying it costs little and the results do not yet show which variant will capture value, so the option stays open.
Standard clinical chambers are core dosimetry products with steady calibration and service revenue, so this multi-model line is a low-risk commitment rather than an option to abandon.
A relative dosimetry chamber complements the water phantoms and the scanning workflow, so it supports the platform strategy at a low cost to maintain.
Thimble chambers are established, widely used devices with predictable demand, and nothing in the early results suggests abandoning this one.
